QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_44

question.text: Value at Risk (VaR) has which of the following limitations?

answer.text: It indicates the exact size of loss beyond the confidence threshold
It tells investors nothing about the probability of loss
It does NOT tell you the size of loss in the tail beyond the confidence level

explanation.text: The Logic: VaR quantifies the maximum expected loss at a given confidence level over a defined horizon, but it does not tell the user the magnitude of loss in the tail beyond that confidence threshold. This is the limitation of VaR called out in the workbook. The Trap: Option A states the opposite of the workbook position. Option B is incorrect because VaR is, by definition, a probabilistic loss measure. Option D introduces an unsupported asymmetry. Note: The limitation that VaR is silent on the size of losses beyond the confidence-level event is the specific point made in the Cat III AIF workbook.
